parallel.requirements: Recognized the exact Rust 2021 C++-to-Rust porting task, byte-for-byte stdout, std-only dependency policy, Cargo project layout, /output/test4.rs entrypoint, and executable requirement.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used the parent as implementation owner while delegating semantic reconstruction to one workflow and later adversarial review to another workflow with multiple child lenses and verifiers.
parallel.implementation: Implemented a from-scratch Rust earcut project with cli, polygon, earcut node/geometry/hole/zorder modules, tests, tools, README, and compiled executable.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Assembled a coherent /output tree and artifact validation copied the expected entrypoint, Cargo files, source modules, tests, tools, and binaries.
parallel.verification: Ran small, broad, edge-case, large-n, cargo, and official evaluator checks; official evaluation completed with 34/34 passing testcases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The late adversarial review workflow was killed before returning an aggregate result, leaving a verified non-UTF-8 argv divergence and other review work unintegrated; final.txt is empty.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same C++ test4 requirements: Rust 2021, std-only, exact CLI parsing, byte-for-byte stdout with trailing spaces, Cargo project structure, and executable output.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all investigation, implementation, verification, integration, and final response in one local agent trajectory with workflows disabled and no subagents.
serial.implementation: Built a compact Rust port with Cargo.toml, test4.rs, and earcut modules for geometry, node arena, and core algorithm.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Produced a coherent /output artifact with expected entrypoint and release binary, then returned a final summary of build and verification evidence.
serial.verification: Compared outputs for n=0..120 plus edge arguments and larger n values, built with cargo release, and official evaluation completed with 34/34 passing testcases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished delegated work or empty final response is visible; clippy was unavailable but rustc/cargo checks and official evaluation passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the C++ test4 porting task, including Rust 2021, exact CLI/default argument behavior, byte-for-byte output formatting, zero external dependencies, module organization, and executable production.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the same prompt and requirements and solved against the same source and oracle constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference in the final artifacts; both passed 34/34 official tests, though the parallel review later exposed a non-UTF-8 argv edge case not integrated before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent used two workflows: an initial spec-reconstruction workflow and a late adversarial review workflow, while retaining implementation ownership in the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run was a single local trajectory with workflows and delegation disabled and zero subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposed research and review across children; serial kept all implementation, verification, and reporting in one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The review workflow brief supplied project location, oracle, hard requirements, known passing ranges, and review-lens instructions to children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used the original task context directly and summarized the same porting constraints and validation in its final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no evidence of a missing child brief or cross-agent interface contract; the main context difference is that parallel had child handoff boundaries while serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent built a larger Cargo project with src modules, tests, tools, README, and a compiled test4 artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run built a more compact Cargo project with an earcut module tree and test4.rs entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented a complete Rust earcut port and passed; parallel added extra parity tooling and README, while serial used a smaller direct module layout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The initial spec workflow completed, but the late review workflow was killed with null aggregate result and unfinished/progress children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run finished normally and returned a final summary after build and differential verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a trapped late review lifecycle after artifact creation; serial had no child lifecycle and closed cleanly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent assembled the final /output tree before the review and artifact validation copied a coherent project with Cargo files, src modules, tests, tools, and executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial artifact validation copied a coherent project with Cargo files, earcut modules, and executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No write collision or contamination explains a task result difference; both final trees were coherent, with parallel carrying additional generated build/test artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran extensive differential tests, Cargo tests, release checks, and official evaluation; a late review also found a non-UTF-8 argv divergence before termination.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran selected differential checks, release Cargo build, and official evaluation, then reported byte-for-byte verification coverage.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both achieved official 34/34 pass; parallel had broader internal verification but failed to integrate the late review finding before timeout, while serial completed its local verification/summary loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel exhausted its run budget: cell metadata marks timed_out true and status records agent returncode 143 after 2444.936 seconds.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 643.89 agent seconds with returncode 0 and no timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete task outcome was the same, but parallel spent the remaining budget on late multi-agent review and closed without a final response; serial closed normally with ample remaining budget.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current completed status.json evaluations show both parallel and serial passed all 34 testcases, so there is no discordant official outcome. The task-solving difference is process-level: serial completed a single-agent implementation and final summary, while parallel produced a passing artifact but then spent the remaining budget in a late adversarial review workflow that never returned an aggregate result.
parallel_contributors: Passing artifact was already built and officially evaluated successfully.
Late review fan-out was adverse to process closure but not to the official pass/fail result.
serial_contributors: Single-agent implementation avoided child lifecycle overhead and returned a normal final response.
Differential and release-build checks were sufficient for official 34/34 success.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel review identified a non-UTF-8 argv panic in the Rust implementation, but this was outside the official testcase surface and was not integrated before timeout.
Serial used a smaller implementation layout and did not run the same late adversarial review.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; one parallel-side adverse process pattern retained
